修复 BashTool 在组合命令中跟踪工作目录不正确的问题。

复现一：临时根目录下有 sub，执行 `cd sub && false`。
cd 已成功，后面的 false 退出码为 1；下一次调用 pwd 应在 sub，目前却仍在根目录。

复现二：执行 `false && cd sub; true`。
cd 因条件不满足从未执行，下一次 pwd 应仍在根目录，目前却可能错误进入 sub。

要求：
1. 跟踪同一次 shell 执行中最终实际到达的目录，不能用整条命令成功与否判断所有 cd 是否执行。
2. 覆盖 && 和分号串联：先 cd 成功再失败、cd 被跳过、多次 cd、后续 cd 失败。
3. 括号子 shell 的目录变化不能影响后续调用；引号内的 cd 文本不应当成命令；带空格路径正常。
4. 原 stdout、stderr、失败退出码和截断/超时/危险命令检查仍保留。内部目录信息不得混入用户正常输出。
5. 不修改 Python 进程的全局 cwd。保持线程局部隔离和 Agent 并行批次的契约：
   各工具从批次开始目录执行，真实发生的目录变化按已有规则合并，即使命令最后失败。
6. 本题验收是 macOS/POSIX 下正常完成的命令；超时或显式 exit 时新目录恢复、完整 shell 语法解析不作为新增要求。
   不应顺带删除或破坏项目已有的 Windows 路由和辅助函数兼容性。
7. 使用本地临时目录写开发测试，不调用真实模型；可新增测试，不修改或删除已有测试。
8. 不读取或修改原项目 baseline 中的外部验收材料。不修复跨文件工具相对路径、空回复、会话、换行或 Agent 实例隔离等其他题。
9. 已有 README 总行数失败不处理；源码变动导致具体文档引用失效时可同步，不改测试放宽标准。

请阅读代码、修复并运行相关测试，最后说明改动、测试结果与未解决限制。
I'll start by exploring the repository structure to find the BashTool implementation.

1	"""Shell command execution with safety checks.
2	
3	Claude Code's BashTool is 1,143 lines. This is the distilled version:
4	- Output capture with truncation (head+tail preserved)
5	- Timeout support
6	- Dangerous command detection
7	- Working directory tracking (cd awareness)
8	"""
9	
10	import os
11	import re
12	import subprocess
13	import threading
14	from typing import ClassVar
15	
16	from ..shell import run_shell
17	from .base import Tool
18	
19	# Track cwd across commands (Claude Code does this too). Thread-local, so that
20	# when the agent executes tools in parallel two bash calls never race on one
21	# shared global: each worker thread carries its own cwd. See article 05.
22	_local = threading.local()
23	
24	
25	def get_tracked_cwd() -> str | None:
26	    """The cwd tracked for this thread, if any."""
27	    return getattr(_local, "cwd", None)
28	
29	
30	def set_tracked_cwd(path: str | None) -> None:
31	    """Set the tracked cwd for this thread (session handoff at pool edges)."""
32	    if path is None:
33	        if hasattr(_local, "cwd"):
34	            del _local.cwd
35	    else:
36	        _local.cwd = path
37	
38	# patterns that could wreck the filesystem or leak secrets
39	_DANGEROUS_PATTERNS = [
40	    # recursive delete aimed at root/home (force flag optional)
41	    (r"\brm\s+(-\w*)?-r\w*\s+(/|~|\$HOME)", "recursive delete on home/root"),
42	    # recursive (-r/-R) and force (-f) flags together, in any order or spacing
43	    (r"\brm\b(?=(?:.*\s)?-\w*[rR])(?=(?:.*\s)?-\w*f)", "force recursive delete"),
44	    # the same, written with long-form flags
45	    (r"\brm\b.*--recursive\b.*--force\b|\brm\b.*--force\b.*--recursive\b", "force recursive delete"),
46	    (r"\bmkfs\b", "format filesystem"),
47	    (r"\bdd\s+.*of=/dev/", "raw disk write"),
48	    (r">\s*/dev/sd[a-z]", "overwrite block device"),
49	    (r"\bchmod\s+(-R\s+)?777\s+/", "chmod 777 on root"),
50	    (r":\(\)\s*\{.*:\|:.*\}", "fork bomb"),
51	    (r"\bcurl\b.*\|\s*(sudo\s+)?(ba)?sh\b", "pipe curl to shell"),
52	    (r"\bwget\b.*\|\s*(sudo\s+)?(ba)?sh\b", "pipe wget to shell"),
53	]
54	
55	
56	class BashTool(Tool):
57	    name = "bash"
58	    description = (
59	        "Execute a shell command. Returns stdout, stderr, and exit code. "
60	        "Use this for running tests, installing packages, git operations, etc."
61	    )
62	    parameters: ClassVar[dict] = {
63	        "type": "object",
64	        "properties": {
65	            "command": {
66	                "type": "string",
67	                "description": "The shell command to run",
68	            },
69	            "timeout": {
70	                "type": "integer",
71	                "description": "Timeout in seconds (default 120)",
72	            },
73	        },
74	        "required": ["command"],
75	    }
76	
77	    def execute(self, command: str, timeout: int = 120) -> str:
78	        # safety check
79	        warning = _check_dangerous(command)
80	        if warning:
81	            return f"⚠ Blocked: {warning}\nCommand: {command}\nIf intentional, modify the command to be more specific."
82	
83	        # use this thread's own tracked working directory
84	        cwd = get_tracked_cwd() or os.getcwd()
85	
86	        try:
87	            proc = run_shell(
88	                command,
89	                check=False,
90	                capture_output=True,
91	                text=True,
92	                encoding="utf-8",
93	                errors="replace",
94	                timeout=timeout,
95	                cwd=cwd,
96	            )
97	
98	            # track cd commands so next command runs in the right place
99	            if proc.returncode == 0:
100	                _update_cwd(command, cwd)
101	            out = proc.stdout
102	            if proc.stderr:
103	                out += f"\n[stderr]\n{proc.stderr}"
104	            if proc.returncode != 0:
105	                out += f"\n[exit code: {proc.returncode}]"
106	            # keep head + tail to preserve the most useful info
107	            if len(out) > 15_000:
108	                out = (
109	                    out[:6000]
110	                    + f"\n\n... truncated ({len(out)} chars total) ...\n\n"
111	                    + out[-3000:]
112	                )
113	            return out.strip() or "(no output)"
114	        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
115	            return f"Error: timed out after {timeout}s"
116	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
117	            # anything else from the OS (spawn failure etc.) also comes back as text
118	            return f"Error running command: {e}"
119	
120	
121	def _check_dangerous(cmd: str) -> str | None:
122	    """Return a warning string if the command looks destructive, else None."""
123	    for pattern, reason in _DANGEROUS_PATTERNS:
124	        if re.search(pattern, cmd):
125	            return reason
126	    return None
127	
128	
129	def _split_words(statement: str) -> list[str]:
130	    """Split one statement into words on unquoted whitespace, stripping the
131	    quotes. Backslashes are kept verbatim (Windows paths must not lose them,
132	    so this deliberately does not use shlex's posix escape processing)."""
133	    words: list[str] = []
134	    buf: list[str] = []
135	    quote: str | None = None
136	    for ch in statement:
137	        if quote is not None:
138	            if ch == quote:
139	                quote = None
140	            else:
141	                buf.append(ch)
142	        elif ch in ("'", '"'):
143	            quote = ch
144	        elif ch.isspace():
145	            if buf:
146	                words.append("".join(buf))
147	                buf = []
148	        else:
149	            buf.append(ch)
150	    if buf:
151	        words.append("".join(buf))
152	    return words
153	
154	
155	def _split_statements(command: str) -> list[list[str]]:
156	    """Split a shell command into per-statement word lists on `&&` and `;`,
157	    honoring quotes. Words come back dequoted, so `cd "my dir"` arrives as
158	    ["cd", "my dir"] and a separator inside quotes never splits."""
159	    statements: list[str] = []
160	    quote: str | None = None
161	    start = 0
162	    i = 0
163	    while i < len(command):
164	        ch = command[i]
165	        if quote is not None:
166	            if ch == quote:
167	                quote = None
168	        elif ch in ("'", '"'):
169	            quote = ch
170	        else:
171	            is_and = command[i : i + 2] == "&&"
172	            if ch == ";" or is_and:
173	                statement = command[start:i]
174	                if statement.strip():
175	                    statements.append(statement)
176	                i += 2 if is_and else 1
177	                start = i
178	                continue
179	        i += 1
180	    tail = command[start:]
181	    if tail.strip():
182	        statements.append(tail)
183	    return [_split_words(statement) for statement in statements]
184	
185	
186	def _update_cwd(command: str, current_cwd: str):
187	    """Track directory changes from cd commands, per thread."""
188	    # walk each cd in a && or ; chain, resolving relative targets against the dir the
189	    # previous cd landed in (not the original cwd) so `cd a && cd b` ends in a/b.
190	    # a parenthesized group is a subshell — `( cd a )` never changes this shell's
191	    # cwd, so scrub those before scanning; a bare `cd` goes home.
192	    scrubbed = re.sub(r"\([^()]*\)", " ", command)
193	    running = current_cwd
194	    changed = False
195	    for words in _split_statements(scrubbed):
196	        if words and words[0] == "cd":
197	            target = words[1] if len(words) > 1 else "~"
198	            new_dir = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(running, os.path.expanduser(target)))
199	            if os.path.isdir(new_dir):
200	                running = new_dir
201	                changed = True
202	    if changed:
203	        _local.cwd = running

1	"""Shell routing: POSIX commands need a POSIX shell.
2	
3	On macOS/Linux `shell=True` already means /bin/sh. On Windows it means
4	cmd.exe, where pwd, ls, cat, sleep and friends do not exist. Every shell
5	spawn in CoreCoder goes through here so Windows gets Git Bash instead.
6	"""
7	
8	import os
9	import re
10	import shutil
11	import subprocess
12	from functools import lru_cache
13	
14	# Drive-letter span: `C:\Users\...` up to a shell metacharacter. Escapes like
15	# `\n` never follow a drive letter, so they pass through untouched.
16	_DRIVE_PATH_RE = re.compile(r"([A-Za-z]):((?:\\[^\s;&|<>()'\"]+)+)")
17	
18	
19	def _posixify_drive_paths(command: str) -> str:
20	    """Rewrite drive-letter paths to git-bash's ``C:/...`` form.
21	
22	    bash's lexer eats backslashes, so an unquoted ``C:\\Users\\runner`` hook
23	    path or ``cd`` target comes out as ``C:Usersrunner`` and the command
24	    fails silently. git-bash accepts the forward-slash form natively, and no
25	    shell escape sequence looks like a drive letter.
26	    """
27	    return _DRIVE_PATH_RE.sub(lambda m: m.group(1) + ":" + m.group(2).replace("\\", "/"), command)
28	
29	
30	@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
31	def _git_bash() -> str | None:
32	    """Locate Git Bash on Windows; None elsewhere or when absent.
33	
34	    System32\\bash.exe is WSL (a different filesystem and environment, not
35	    the Git installation the user's commands target), so it is never picked.
36	    """
37	    if os.name != "nt":
38	        return None
39	    candidate = os.path.join(
40	        os.environ.get("ProgramFiles", r"C:\Program Files"), "Git", "bin", "bash.exe"
41	    )
42	    if os.path.isfile(candidate):
43	        return candidate
44	    git = shutil.which("git")
45	    if git:
46	        derived = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(git)), "bin", "bash.exe")
47	        if os.path.isfile(derived):
48	            return derived
49	    return None
50	
51	
52	def run_shell(command: str, check: bool = False, **kwargs) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
53	    """Run one POSIX command string, via Git Bash on Windows when present.
54	
55	    The list form bypasses cmd.exe entirely; without Git Bash we fall back
56	    to the platform default (cmd.exe on Windows, /bin/sh elsewhere).
57	    """
58	    bash = _git_bash()
59	    if bash is not None:
60	        return subprocess.run([bash, "-c", _posixify_drive_paths(command)], shell=False, check=check, **kwargs)
61	    return subprocess.run(command, shell=True, check=check, **kwargs)

./article/02-tools_EN.md:146:The other two things deserve a passing mention. Output truncation keeps head and tail: when a command spews tens of thousands of lines, only the first 6000 and last 3000 characters are kept, with one line of explanation standing in for the middle, which neither blows up the context nor loses the most useful opening and ending. Working-directory tracking lets `cd` be remembered across commands, and `_update_cwd` specially handles chained jumps like `cd a && cd b`, resolving b relative to a rather than relative to the starting point (the test `test_bash_chained_cd_resolves_sequentially` watches it). 170	    def _exec_tools_parallel(self, tool_calls, on_tool=None) -> list[str]:
171	        """Run multiple tool calls concurrently using threads.
172	
173	        This is inspired by Claude Code's StreamingToolExecutor which starts
174	        executing tools while the model is still generating.  We simplify to:
175	        when the model returns N tool calls at once, run them in parallel.
176	        """
177	        from .tools.bash import get_tracked_cwd, set_tracked_cwd
178	
179	        for tc in tool_calls:
180	            if on_tool:
181	                on_tool(tc.name, tc.arguments)
182	
183	        # hooks and consent are settled up front on this thread: prompting
184	        # from pool workers would interleave several prompts on one terminal
185	        results = [self._pre_hooks(tc) or self._permit(tc) for tc in tool_calls]
186	        # the tracked cwd is thread-local, so pool workers would otherwise
187	        # start from the launch directory: hand the session cwd in, and merge
188	        # any cd back in call order so the batch behaves like a sequence
189	        session_cwd = get_tracked_cwd()
190	        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool:
191	            def run(i, tc, base_cwd):
192	                is_bash = tc.name == "bash"
193	                if is_bash and base_cwd is not None:
194	                    set_tracked_cwd(base_cwd)
195	                out = self._exec_tool(tc)
196	                if not is_bash:
197	                    return i, out, None
198	                cwd_after = get_tracked_cwd()
199	                # only a worker that actually moved the dir reports back; a
200	                # sibling that merely inherited the base must not revert a cd
201	                return i, out, cwd_after if cwd_after != base_cwd else None
202	
203	            futures = {
204	                i: pool.submit(run, i, tc, session_cwd)
205	                for i, tc in enumerate(tool_calls)
206	                if results[i] is None
207	            }
208	            for i, future in futures.items():
209	                i, results[i], worker_cwd = future.result()
210	                if worker_cwd is not None:
211	                    session_cwd = worker_cwd
212	                    set_tracked_cwd(worker_cwd)
213	        for i in futures:
214	            self._post_hooks(tool_calls[i], results[i])
215	        return results
